# @darcysm/bastet-ui

> A modern, accessible, multi-themed React component library built with TypeScript, Radix UI primitives, and a zero-dependency Native CSS Token Engine.

## Overview

`@darcysm/bastet-ui` provides accessible, high-performance UI components with first-class theme switching. Components are unstyled at the logic layer via Radix UI primitives and styled with scoped CSS Modules powered by CSS custom properties.

- **Package**: `@darcysm/bastet-ui`
- **Version**: `0.2.0`
- **Framework**: React 18+ / React 19+
- **Styling**: Scoped CSS Modules + CSS Custom Properties (No Tailwind, No runtime CSS-in-JS, No Ant Design)
- **Accessibility**: WAI-ARIA compliant via Radix UI primitives (`@radix-ui/react-*`)
- **Theme Presets**: 6 built-in themes (Light, Dark, Oriental, Black Metal, Pink, Popayán Ciudad Blanca)

---

## Installation

```bash
# npm
npm install @darcysm/bastet-ui

# bun
bun add @darcysm/bastet-ui

# pnpm
pnpm add @darcysm/bastet-ui

# yarn
yarn add @darcysm/bastet-ui
```

### Peer Dependencies
Ensure `react` and `react-dom` are installed in your project:
```bash
npm install react react-dom
```

---

## Quick Start

### 1. Import CSS Styles
Import the library styles once in your root layout or entry file (`App.tsx`, `main.tsx`, or `layout.tsx`):

```tsx
import '@darcysm/bastet-ui/styles.css';
```

### 2. Wrap your application with `BstThemeProvider`

```tsx
import React from 'react';
import { BstThemeProvider, Button } from '@darcysm/bastet-ui';
import '@darcysm/bastet-ui/styles.css';

export default function App() {
  return (
    <BstThemeProvider themeName="dark">
      <main>
        <Button variant="primary">Hello Bastet UI</Button>
      </main>
    </BstThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

---

## Theme System

### Available Theme Presets
The library includes 6 curated themes:

| `ThemeName` | Description | Typical Palette |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `'light'` | Crisp modern light theme | Clean slate, vibrant purple primary |
| `'dark'` | Deep dark theme | Dark obsidian background, bright accent |
| `'oriental'` | Asian-inspired aesthetic | Warm crimson reds, jade greens, soft paper |
| `'black-metal'` | High-contrast monochromatic | Pure dark backgrounds, stark silver/white accents |
| `'pink'` | Vibrant playful palette | Bubblegum pinks, magenta, soft pastels |
| `'popayan-ciudad-blanca'` | Colonial Popayán heritage | White facades, colonial tile brown/gold, Cinzel serif typography |

### `useBstTheme` Hook
Access and toggle themes dynamically anywhere in your component tree:

```tsx
import { useBstTheme, Button } from '@darcysm/bastet-ui';

function ThemeControls() {
  const { currentTheme, setTheme, themeNames, tokens } = useBstTheme();

  return (
    <div>
      <p>Current: {currentTheme}</p>
      <Button onClick={() => setTheme('popayan-ciudad-blanca')}>
        Switch to Ciudad Blanca
      </Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Custom Token Overrides
You can customize design tokens when initializing `BstThemeProvider`:

```tsx
<BstThemeProvider
  themeName="dark"
  customTokens={{
    colorPrimary: '#8b5cf6',
    borderRadius: 8,
  }}
>
  <App />
</BstThemeProvider>
```

---

## Core Components Reference

### 1. Button
Polymorphic, accessible button supporting `@radix-ui/react-slot` composition via `asChild`.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@darcysm/bastet-ui';

// Standard button
<Button variant="primary" size="medium" onClick={() => console.log('clicked')}>
  Click Me
</Button>

// Variants: 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'tertiary' | 'outline' | 'ghost' | 'danger'
// Sizes: 'small' | 'medium' | 'large'
// States: loading, disabled, fullWidth

// Composition with asChild (e.g. Next.js Link or React Router Link)
<Button asChild variant="outline">
  <a href="/projects">Go to Projects</a>
</Button>
```

### 2. Select
Accessible dropdown select powered by `@radix-ui/react-select`. Includes automatic collision detection and mobile-friendly viewport bounding.

```tsx
import { Select } from '@darcysm/bastet-ui';

const options = [
  { value: 'en', label: 'English' },
  { value: 'es', label: 'Español' },
  { value: 'fr', label: 'Français', disabled: true },
];

function LanguageSelector() {
  const [lang, setLang] = React.useState('es');

  return (
    <Select
      label="Choose Language"
      value={lang}
      onChange={setLang}
      options={options}
      placeholder="Select an option"
      size="medium" // 'small' | 'medium' | 'large'
    />
  );
}
```

### 3. Modal
Dialog modal powered by `@radix-ui/react-dialog`. Accessible with automatic focus trapping, escape key dismiss, and smooth overlay backdrop.

```tsx
import { Modal, Button } from '@darcysm/bastet-ui';

function ContactModal() {
  const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = React.useState(false);

  return (
    <>
      <Button onClick={() => setIsOpen(true)}>Open Modal</Button>
      <Modal
        open={isOpen}
        onOpenChange={setIsOpen}
        title="Get in Touch"
        description="Send a message directly to my inbox."
        size="medium" // 'small' | 'medium' | 'large' | 'full'
        footer={
          <>
            <Button variant="ghost" onClick={() => setIsOpen(false)}>Cancel</Button>
            <Button variant="primary" onClick={() => setIsOpen(false)}>Confirm</Button>
          </>
        }
      >
        <p>Modal body content goes here.</p>
      </Modal>
    </>
  );
}
```

### 4. Dropdown
Context/action menu powered by `@radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu`. Automatically detects boundaries so it never clips off-screen on mobile.

```tsx
import { Dropdown, Button } from '@darcysm/bastet-ui';

function UserMenu() {
  const items = [
    { id: 'profile', label: 'Profile', onClick: () => navigate('/profile') },
    { id: 'settings', label: 'Settings', onClick: () => navigate('/settings') },
    { id: 'sep-1', label: '', separator: true },
    { id: 'logout', label: 'Log out', danger: true, onClick: () => logout() },
  ];

  return (
    <Dropdown
      trigger={<Button variant="ghost">Options ▾</Button>}
      items={items}
      placement="bottom-end"
    />
  );
}
```

### 5. Tooltip
Accessible tooltip powered by `@radix-ui/react-tooltip` with dynamic arrow and collision padding.

```tsx
import { Tooltip, Button } from '@darcysm/bastet-ui';

<Tooltip content="Copy link to clipboard" placement="top">
  <Button variant="outline">Share</Button>
</Tooltip>
```

### 6. Card
Flexible container card with optional header, body, footer, and image cover.

```tsx
import { Card, CardHeader, CardBody, CardFooter, Button } from '@darcysm/bastet-ui';

<Card hoverable bordered>
  <CardHeader title="Project Title" extra={<Button size="small">Visit</Button>} />
  <CardBody>
    <p>Card description and content details.</p>
  </CardBody>
  <CardFooter>
    <span>Updated 2 days ago</span>
  </CardFooter>
</Card>
```

### 7. Badge
Status, count, and tag badges.

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@darcysm/bastet-ui';

// Status badge
<Badge status="success" text="Online" />

// Count badge on elements
<Badge count={5}>
  <div style={{ width: 40, height: 40, background: '#eee' }} />
</Badge>

// Tag variant
<Badge variant="pill" color="primary">React</Badge>
```

### 8. Typography (`Heading` & `Text`)
Responsive typography with semantic HTML rendering and responsive fluid clamping.

```tsx
import { Heading, Text } from '@darcysm/bastet-ui';

// Headings
<Heading as="h1" size="2xl" weight="bold">
  Portfolio Title
</Heading>

// Text
<Text variant="secondary" size="medium">
  Frontend Developer specializing in high-performance web applications.
</Text>
```

### 9. FormField (`Input` & `Textarea`)
Form inputs with accessible labels, helper text, and error states.

```tsx
import { Input, Textarea } from '@darcysm/bastet-ui';

<Input
  label="Email Address"
  placeholder="you@example.com"
  type="email"
  required
  helperText="We will never share your email."
/>

<Textarea
  label="Message"
  placeholder="Type your message..."
  rows={4}
/>
```

### 10. Toast Notification System
Lightweight notification system with `ToastProvider` and `useToast`.

```tsx
import { ToastProvider, useToast, Button } from '@darcysm/bastet-ui';

// Wrap near app root:
// <ToastProvider position="bottom-right"><App /></ToastProvider>

function TriggerButton() {
  const { showToast } = useToast();

  return (
    <Button
      onClick={() =>
        showToast({
          title: 'Message sent!',
          type: 'success', // 'success' | 'error' | 'info' | 'warning'
          duration: 3000,
        })
      }
    >
      Send
    </Button>
  );
}
```

### 11. Theme & Language Switchers
Ready-to-use controls for theme and locale switching:

```tsx
import { ThemeSwitcher, LanguageSwitcher } from '@darcysm/bastet-ui';

<ThemeSwitcher size="medium" />
<LanguageSwitcher
  currentLanguage="es"
  onLanguageChange={(lang) => setLocale(lang)}
  options={[
    { code: 'es', label: 'Español' },
    { code: 'en', label: 'English' },
  ]}
/>
```

---

## Design System Rules & Best Practices

1. **Always import `@darcysm/bastet-ui/styles.css` once** at the application entrypoint.
2. **Never apply hardcoded positioning overrides** to Radix portaled components (`Modal`, `Dropdown`, `Tooltip`, `Select`). They compute collision-aware floating coordinates dynamically.
3. **Use `asChild` for router links:** Use `<Button asChild><Link href="...">...</Link></Button>` to avoid nested clickable element issues.
4. **Use CSS variables for theme-aware custom styling:**
   - `--bst-color-primary`
   - `--bst-color-bg-base`
   - `--bst-color-text-base`
   - `--bst-border-radius-base`
   - `--bst-font-family-base`
   - `--bst-font-family-heading`

---

## AI Assistant Prompt Instructions

When generating code using `@darcysm/bastet-ui`:
- Import components directly from `'@darcysm/bastet-ui'`.
- Do **not** import from `antd` or `@ant-design/*`; Bastet UI does not depend on Ant Design.
- Use `BstThemeProvider` with one of the valid `themeName` strings: `'light'`, `'dark'`, `'oriental'`, `'black-metal'`, `'pink'`, `'popayan-ciudad-blanca'`.
- For `Select`, pass `options={[{ value: 'val', label: 'Label' }]}` and `onChange={(val) => ...}`.
- For `Modal`, pass `open`, `onOpenChange`, `title`, and optional `footer`.
- For `Dropdown`, pass `trigger={<Element />}` and `items={[{ id: '1', label: 'Text', onClick: fn }]}`.
